product: Cartesia — speech to text, realtime (Ink WebSocket)

source_audio.description: No audio was submitted and no request was issued: this frame is authored to Cartesia's published realtime speech-to-text protocol documentation, not captured from the service. The transcript is a fictional Spanish sentence authored for this repository ('La llamada quedó registrada en el sistema.'), written in the same style as the Spanish fixtures already committed to this tree; it names no real person, organisation, number, date or reference, and no voice — synthetic or otherwise — was involved.

redaction.notes: Nothing was redacted because nothing was captured. request_id holds the nil GUID — the placeholder form protocol section 4 prescribes for a correlating identifier — because no real request exists to identify.

terms.basis: docs/guides/provider-recording-protocol.md section 7 — no Output was captured at all; the fixture is authored to Cartesia's published protocol documentation. Cartesia's own verdict for a capture is permitted-with-conditions, and it is not what blocks one here (see notes)

source_schema.method: The documented field set, nesting, types and cardinality of the realtime speech-to-text transcript message were read from the page above and corroborated against https://docs.cartesia.ai/api-reference/stt/stt, which documents the same four server message types. The frame conforms to that schema: type, request_id, text, is_final, duration and words[] (word, start, end), with word timings in seconds as documented. The 'language' field is carried because the documentation's response example shows it on the transcript message, even though it is not enumerated in that page's schema property list — a divergence inside the vendor's own page, recorded here rather than silently resolved either way. No vendor example payload, prose or field description was copied into this repository — only the documented field names and the literal message-type constant 'transcript', which is interface, not expression. Every value is our own fiction.

notes: Final frame: is_final true, the shape Cartesia sends once a segment is settled. WHY THIS IS DOCUMENTATION-DERIVED RATHER THAN CAPTURED, and it is NOT a terms problem: section 7 of the protocol guide records Cartesia as permitted-with-conditions — its ToS section 5.3(b) expressly permits use of Output outside the Services and its AUP carries no sharing restriction — so the terms would have permitted a real capture of this frame on a commercial-use tier. The reason there is no capture is simply that NO CAPTURE CREDENTIAL EXISTS IN THIS ENVIRONMENT. A real capture is therefore a known, cleared upgrade path for this provider the moment a credential appears: re-run section 3 of the guide in full, on a commercial-use tier, and replace this file with a class 'recorded' one. THE FIELD THIS FIXTURE DOES NOT CARRY IS THE POINT: Cartesia documents no 'confidence' field on the transcript message and no per-word confidence, yet the SDK models CartesiaSttTranscriptMessage.Confidence as a nullable float and falls back to 0f. This fixture is schema-faithful and therefore omits it, which is what makes that fallback assertable. What this artifact is worth, stated plainly: a documented schema is what the vendor says it sends, whereas a capture is what it actually sent on one day. This route closes the field-set and frame-ordering half of the ADR-0041 D4 gap and cannot close the does-the-vendor-honour-its-own-docs half. The page publishes no revision marker, so a silent breaking edit there is indistinguishable from no edit at all — re-read the source_schema URL first when this suite starts failing.
